introduction_markdown: You are required to answer FIVE questions, choosing THREE from Section A and TWO from Section B. All the questions carry equal marks and marks allocated to parts of questions are indicated. Extra questions answered from each section shall NOT be marked. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. Duration: two and a half hours.
enonce_intro_markdown: In what ways are the following institutions important to the community?
incertitudes: Le PDF compte 3 pages (page de garde, Section A, Section B) ; rien ne manque. Scan sans couche texte lu en image ; filigranes gcerevision.com (Kawlo) ignorés. Page de garde vérifiée : GCE Board, JUNE 2026, ORDINARY LEVEL, Human Biology, Paper 2, code 0565, durée deux heures et demie.

Choix : la page de garde dit de répondre à 5 questions, 3 de la Section A et 2 de la Section B. Traduit en regles_choix : SECTION A 3 sur 5, SECTION B 2 sur 4. Les questions de la Section B sont numérotées 6 à 9 sur le sujet (numero_exercice B6 à B9).
Points imprimés par sous-partie recopiés tels quels ; points d'une sous-question = somme des points du bloc lettré ; chaque question totalise 20 (« Total=20 marks »), ce qui est cohérent.

Aucun corrigé officiel : tous les corrigés sont rédigés. Aucune figure du sujet à extraire : les schémas demandés (Q1 a, Q2 b, Q5 a) sont à dessiner par le candidat ; le corrigé décrit les éléments et les légendes attendus.
Q9 (a) : le sujet glose « Sanatorium » par « home for mental patients » ; recopié et traité tel quel (le mot désigne ailleurs un établissement pour tuberculeux).

questions.corrige_markdown:
1. It provides **care and treatment** for mentally ill patients, by trained doctors, nurses and psychiatrists.
2. It **protects** the patients from harming themselves and others, and protects them from neglect, abuse and rejection by the community.
3. It helps patients to **recover and return** to normal life through therapy and rehabilitation.
4. It reduces the **stigma** attached to mental illness, and relieves families of the burden of caring for them.

1. It provides **treatment** (multidrug therapy) and care for leprosy patients, which cures the disease and stops it from spreading.
2. It prevents **deformities and disabilities** through early treatment, physiotherapy and surgery.
3. It offers **rehabilitation** (vocational training, skills) so that patients can earn a living and return to the community.
4. It provides **health education** and reduces the **stigma** and discrimination against the patients.

1. They give **spiritual and moral guidance**, teaching honesty, respect and good behaviour.
2. They help to reduce **social vices** (theft, drug abuse, prostitution, violence).
3. They run **schools, hospitals and health centres**, and carry out health education.
4. They give **charity and help** to the poor, orphans, widows and the sick.
5. They offer **counselling** and comfort in times of trouble, and unite people of different backgrounds, promoting peace and community spirit.

1. They **diagnose and treat** diseases and injuries, using laboratory tests and X-rays.
2. They provide **emergency care** and **surgery**, saving lives after accidents.
3. They provide **maternity services**: antenatal care, safe delivery and postnatal care for mothers and babies.
4. They carry out **immunisation** and other **preventive services** (family planning, screening).
5. They provide **health education** to the community on hygiene, nutrition and disease prevention.
6. They **train** doctors, nurses and other health workers, and carry out **research** and disease **surveillance**.
7. They keep **blood banks** and a pharmacy, and **refer** difficult cases to specialised centres; they also provide employment.
